summary.text: A 47-year-old woman was admitted to the Emergency Department with persistent cough, dyspnea, fatigue and severe back pain, and had self-detected a painless left breast lump 4 months before hospitalization. Examination showed a roughly 6 cm hard left breast lump with peau d’orange change and nipple deviation, a 2-cm left axillary node, afebrile status and ECOG 2.

Complete blood count showed WBC 21.83 G/L, hemoglobin 87 g/L and platelets 22 G/L. Full-body CT showed multi-organ metastasis and lung consolidation suggesting pneumonitis; core needle biopsy showed grade 3 invasive ductal carcinoma of no special type and bone marrow aspiration showed malignant infiltration. Diagnosis was pneumonitis and left breast cancer cT4N3M1 with bone marrow invasion resulting in pancytopenia.

She received platelet infusions and antibiotics, then doxorubicin-cyclophosphamide chemotherapy with zoledronic acid and a 20% dose reduction in the first cycle. Platelets recovered after the first cycle, her complete blood count returned to normal, back pain was relieved and the breast tumor reduced in size. After completing chemotherapy she was switched to goserelin, anastrozole and zoledronic acid, and the breast tumor became undetectable.

After 14 months of stable disease she developed jaundice, dyspnea and increased back pain, with CT progression in bone, lungs and liver, and was switched to second-line paclitaxel. After 6 months of paclitaxel the disease progressed with brain metastasis. The patient died with an overall survival of 21 months.
